missions.name: Apollo 11
missions.summary: First human landing on the Moon. The descent stage remains on the surface.
key_discoveries: First successful human landing on another world
Confirmed the lunar surface could support a spacecraft
Laser reflector still used today to measure Earth-Moon distance
missions.why_it_matters: The descent stage and retroreflector remain on the Moon. The reflector is still used by scientists to measure the distance between Earth and the Moon with high precision.
missions.story: On 20 July 1969 the Lunar Module Eagle landed in the Sea of Tranquility. After the moonwalk, the ascent stage lifted off, leaving the descent stage and scientific instruments on the surface. Those pieces of hardware are still there.

images.alt: Apollo 11 Lunar Module on the Moon

missions.name: Viking 1 Lander
missions.status: Silent / Abandoned on the surface of Mars
missions.summary: First successful soft landing on Mars. Operated for more than six years.
key_discoveries: First successful soft landing on Mars
First detailed surface images of Mars
missions.why_it_matters: Viking 1 proved soft landings on Mars were possible and delivered the first long-term scientific data from the Martian surface. Later missions built on its lessons.
missions.story: Viking 1 landed on Mars in July 1976. Designed for 90 days, it operated for more than six years. It sent the first high-resolution images of the Martian surface and ran biology experiments. Contact was lost in 1982. The lander remains on the surface.

images.alt: First clear image from the surface of Mars by Viking 1
